transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

Yes — a gradual loss of suction is usually recoverable, so I would not replace it yet. The most likely cause is a clogged filter, followed by a blockage in the hose/wand or floorhead. Unplug it, remove the washable filters and check them: if dusty, rinse in cold water only, squeeze gently and leave them to air-dry completely for at least 24 hours before refitting; a damp filter will restrict airflow. Can you check whether the filters are dirty or damp?
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
Never washed them, didn't know they were there. The foam one is solid grey and the felt one is caked with fine dust. No burning smell, by the way.

Those filters are very likely the main reason for the loss of suction. Rinse the foam and felt filters repeatedly in cold water only until the water runs clear; do not use detergent or heat. Gently squeeze out the water and leave them somewhere warm and ventilated for at least 24 hours, longer if they still feel cool or damp, before refitting—using it with damp filters can restrict airflow and risk the motor. Once fully dry, test it on hard floor. If suction is still weak after that, the next likely cause is a blockage in the hose, wand or floorhead rather than a reason to replace the vacuum.
Ok, will wash them and leave them 24 hours. Is there anything else I should check while I wait?

Yes. With it unplugged, detach the hose/wand and floorhead if they come apart normally, then look through each airway towards a light. Check the inlet where the hose meets the bin and the narrow neck above the floorhead; remove any loose blockage you can reach, but do not force tools into the hose. Turn the floorhead over and remove any hair or thread around the brush bar, then make sure it turns freely by hand. Once the filters are completely dry, refit them and test on hard floor: if suction is still weak, a hidden blockage or an air leak at a seal becomes more likely.

Ok. Checked the hose, a coin drops straight through and no splits. Wand is clear, I can see light through it. Brushroll has a bit of fluff but spins freely. Suction is weak at the end of the hose too.

The heavily clogged filters are still the leading cause; because suction is weak at the hose end as well, the brushroll is not the main issue. While they dry, unplug the vacuum, remove the bin normally and inspect the inlet where the hose feeds into it, plus the cyclone/separator cone above the bin, for compacted dust. Tip out or gently brush away only loose debris you can reach—do not poke tools into narrow passages or dismantle the motor unit. When the filters are fully dry and refitted, test again; if it remains weak, a blocked cyclone/airway or a bin/filter seal not seating properly becomes the next likely cause.
Not sure what the cyclone part looks like, to be honest. The rubber seal on the bin looks fine though. Is that what you meant?

Yes — the rubber seal around the bin is one of the seals I meant, and if it looks sound and sits evenly it is less likely to be the cause. The cyclone/separator is the fixed plastic cone or shroud immediately above the bin: it is the part dirt-laden air passes through before reaching the filters, often with slots, holes or a grille around it. With the vacuum unplugged and the bin removed normally, look up into that area for a ring of compacted fine dust or fluff. You can tip or gently brush off loose material you can reach, but do not prise it apart or push anything into narrow openings. The unwashed, heavily grey filters remain the most likely explanation; once they are fully dry and refitted, the hard-floor test will tell us whether there is anything further to chase.
Ok, had a look up there. Can't really tell what I'm looking at, but nothing obvious. I'll wait for the filters to dry and test it then.

That is the right point to stop checking for now. The filters are still by far the most likely cause: the clear hose and wand, freely turning brushroll, sound-looking bin seal and lack of an obvious obstruction all make a simple airflow restriction at the filters most likely. Do not refit them at the 24-hour mark if either still feels cool or damp; leave them longer. Once they are fully dry, refit them and test on hard floor. If suction is still weak at the hose end after that, the remaining likely causes are a restriction in the cyclone/internal air path or, less commonly, an internal motor-airflow fault, which would need an engineer rather than replacing the vacuum straight away.
